answer: Because the quill height is fixed at intake and written down in the beacon receipt, the shale audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 812 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
